name: Dylan Brady
notes: Hyperpop producer working by file-exchange, colliding incompatible tempo grammars inside one track, and one of the fully documented entries here — DAW, remote workflow, the switch-driven method and the genre inventory are all sourced. The research is explicit that the switch, not any one groove, is the parameter: "BPM 90—200 within a single song — ska/pop-punk at 150—180, nightcore at 160—175, dubstep half-time at 140, happy hardcore at 170—180; the backbeat placement changes with each switch, which is the point." A single `placement` field cannot change with a section, so the switch is carried where it can be: `switchUpProb` is 0.5 — the highest number in this whole section — `fills.smallEveryBars` is 2, the section lengths are 4—8 bars, and `kick.densityPerBar` runs 2—8 to span a ska upstroke and a blast beat in one range. The straight class is encoded because it is the one the pop-punk and hardcore modes share. "Clipping and over-limiting are intentional" is the highest velocity tier table authored here plus a hard-transient snare, and "whichever kit the current section demands … cut together hard with no transitions" is why `fillBeforeSection` is false: a jump cut has no fill. The 808 is authored because the entry names it: "distorted 808s, dubstep LFO growl bass and pop-punk electric bass all appear; the bass is the loudest and most distorted element", so `bass808` is `counter_riff` at `saturated` distortion — the only saturated setting in this section — while the pop-punk electric bass stays as an `independent_riff` bassline. Harmony is "minor keys with power-chord and pop-punk diatonic harmony, interrupted by chromatic or atonal interjections", so the families are plain, `triad` is high and `halfStepDissonance` and `susOrDimProb` carry the interjections. "Pitch-shifted, heavily Auto-Tuned vocals as the constant across switches" is the melody timbre and the high `octaveJumpProb`. ⚠ The INFERRED parameters are every drum probability, the velocity tiers, the humanize pair and `bpm.mode` 165 (the research gives four named sub-tempos inside 90—200 and no single centre; 165 is the overlap of the nightcore and happy-hardcore bands, which are the two it names most often). ⚠ The entry's own [LOW-CONF] mark on the harmonic claim is repeated here. ⚠ **The countermelody reached 896/1000 distinct answers against a floor of 980 (2026-08-17, counter variety floor).** The 1-bar value came out of `melody.phraseBars`, which is now [2,4] weighted [3,4]. `generators::melody` writes a phrase's rhythm **once** and reuses it for every repeat, so a 1-bar phrase gives the whole clip one bar of rhythmic entropy — and the counter, whose onsets are read off the lead's, inherits that ceiling. Distinctness is combinatorial in the shape LENGTH, not in the option count. ⚠ The value that moved here is INFERRED rather than a researched claim — the entry's Melody/chords line reads "pitch-shifted, heavily Auto-Tuned vocals as the constant across switches (deliberately reduced on the later album); the palette is drawn from "pop punk, nightcore, ska, dubstep, deconstructed club, trance, metal and happy hardcore". Brady produces in Logic Pro and the duo exchange Logic project files — the documented method is "an exquisite corpse type thing" with "almost an improv mentality".", and every claim in it still holds after the change.
